study.dataset: Grand Challenge knee implant measurements republished by Harba et al. · Grand Challenge fifth competition, five normal walking trials
study.summary: For fast treadmill, the early external adduction moment rose 106%. Measured medial load changed by -0.03 BW. The mechanics model estimated 0.15 BW.

sources.label: Grand Challenge knee implant measurements republished by Harba et al. · MIT (ReducePoly_forMSK); see HARBA-LICENSE.txt.

Grand Challenge fifth competition, five normal walking trials · GPL-3.0 derived dataset from the Modenese et al. reproducibility repository. See GC5-LICENSE.txt for attribution and original data origin.

methods: The study samples 65,536 parameter sets per participant and retains 512 using only designated ordinary-walking implant force traces. Parameters are paired across conditions.

The prescribed-motion model balances sagittal and frontal knee moments with bounded extensor and flexor groups, a paired co-contraction term, and nonnegative medial and lateral contact forces. Geometry uses angle-dependent group leverage from Rajagopal2016. Missing flexion uses 15°.

The two-moment comparator is a linear fit from external knee adduction and absolute external flexion moments. The audit also reports the adduction-only fit and an uncalibrated mechanics reference. All fits use the same calibration subset.

Peaks are the maximum force in 5–45% and 55–95% stance. Mean load is integrated over normalized stance. Where physical stance time is available, force is also integrated in BW·s. Held-out waveform scores use 5–95% stance.

Bands describe the central 90% of retained scenarios under the stated parameter ranges. They measure sensitivity to model assumptions. The offload share counts scenarios with a reduction of at least 0.10 body weights. Departures from sagittal or frontal moment balance greater than 0.005 BW·m are counted.

The 3D study pose drives the generic atlas knee with mean sagittal knee flexion from the input inverse kinematics at each stance phase. The geometry and other joint motions follow the reference atlas.
One participant with a force-measuring right knee replacement, 65 kg and 1.66 m as reported by Harba et al.
Four original recordings yield seven right stances. Two stances per overground recording are repeated measurements from the same walking pass.
The treadmill recording varies both speed and surface. Its direct comparison with natural overground walking cannot isolate either effect.
Each stance is delimited by 20 N crossings on the measured right vertical ground-reaction trace and resampled linearly to 101 points.
Medial (PM + AM) and lateral (AL + PL) implant signals use the source's compartment sums, lbf-to-newton conversion, and 6 Hz forward-backward filter. Total is their compressive sum.

Knee angle and moments come from source inverse kinematics and inverse dynamics. The right knee coordinate is negative in flexion, so its positive internal extension moment corresponds to positive external flexion. The reported external adduction moment reverses the internal adduction sign.
compressionBw is the signed net proximal force from OpenSim inverse dynamics (knee_ty_force), whereas grfBw is the vertical force plate measurement. They are separate inputs.
One normal stance is labeled for calibration. All other stances are evaluation data; the second normal stance is from the same recording.
One left eTibia recipient, five repetitions of normal walking only.
Calibration uses the three lowest-numbered trials (ss1, ss3, ss8). The other two trials (ss9 and ss11) are held out.

Inputs are published force-plate data and OpenSim fitted poses. Knee moments include the ground reaction wrench about the fitted left knee projected on tibial axes, without segment inertia or gravity. Vertical ground reaction approximates external axial compression.

The supplement has whole-cycle implant observations without sample timestamps. Aligned by normalised phase within the matching motion trial, then cropped at 20 N vertical force. The resulting phase match is approximate.

Medial and lateral are published implant-derived compartment forces. Negative compartment estimates are excluded from compartment scoring. Total axial force is the sum of both estimates before exclusion, distinct from the published 3-D magnitude.
